parole.testo: From French apophonie, from Ancient Greek ἀπο- (apo-, “away, from, off”) + φωνή (phōnḗ, “sound”). See also אַבְּלָאוּט (“ablaut”).
Borrowed from French dynamique and reinforced by other descendants, from Ancient Greek δυναμικός (dunamikós, “able, powerful”). Compare דִּינָמִי (dinámi, “dynamic”, adjective).

parole.testo: From French télévision, from télé- (from Ancient Greek τῆλε (têle, “distant”)) + vision (from Latin visio (“vision”)). Use of ־יה suffix is ultimately of Slavic origin; compare Polish telewizja.
